books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the account of Lowell mill workers in the course books. The facts are as stated in the books; the wording is original.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase: In the mill town of Lowell, Massachusetts, young women from farm families worked in textile mills, tending power looms for long hours in exchange for wages. Mill owners housed them in company boardinghouses and set rules for their conduct. Many of the women used their wages to help their families and to save for the future.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The Lowell boardinghouse rules, which set standards for the mill women’s conduct, most directly show that mill owners

options.text: treated the women as enslaved workers.
options.misconception: Background from the books: the women were free to leave, earned wages, and saved money; rules are not slavery, and the passage shows a wage bargain.

options.text: promoted a moral order for respectable working women.
refused to house their workers at all.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the women were free to leave, earned wages, and saved money; rules are not slavery, and the passage shows a wage bargain.
rationales.B: Company housing with conduct rules shows owners selling more than a job: a supervised, respectable life for young women away from home.
rationales.C: The passage says the owners housed the women in company boardinghouses; the rules governed that housing, they did not abolish it.
rationales.D: The women earned wages and used them to help their families; land was not their pay.
rationales.general:
1. Read the bargain: wages and a bed, in exchange for hours at the loom and rules for conduct.
2. Ask what the rules protect: the owners’ claim that mill work was respectable for farm daughters.
3. Name the order: a moral system wrapped around factory work, meant to reassure families back home.
Remember: when a workplace writes rules for life outside work, it is selling respectability as well as wages.
